verdict: Travelers earned $1.9B in Q3 as strong underwriting — an 86.8% combined ratio — and record investment income more than covered $538M of catastrophe losses.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total revenues $12.4B, flat vs a year ago

kpis.label: Combined ratio
kpis.note: claims + expenses took 87 cents per premium dollar

segments.name: Premiums earned
segments.note: Premiums from business, bond & specialty and personal insurance policies, earned over the coverage period — essentially flat, as growth in Business and Bond & Specialty offset the sale of the Canadian personal lines business.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the money Travelers invests between collecting premiums and paying claims — a record $1,098M, up 6%.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.note: Fees for services such as claim handling for other insurers.

segments.name: Other revenues & realized losses
segments.note: Other revenues of $122M, less $34M of net realized investment losses on the portfolio.

opex.name: Amortization of deferred acquisition costs
opex.note: Commissions and other costs of winning policies, spread over the policies' lives.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — staff, offices and systems.

takeaways.title: Underwriting stayed strong
takeaways.text: The combined ratio was 86.8% (84.1% excluding catastrophes and reserve development), and pre-tax underwriting income was $1,432M — profitable insurance, not just investment gains.

takeaways.title: Investments set a record
takeaways.text: Net investment income hit a record $1,098M before tax, up 6%, as higher yields and a larger portfolio lifted what Travelers earns on premiums held before claims are paid.

takeaways.title: Storms cost more than last year
takeaways.text: Catastrophe losses were $538M before tax, up from $402M a year ago, mostly severe wind and hail. Favorable reserve development of $234M — past claims costing less than reserved — more than offset the increase.

oneTimers: Net favorable prior-year reserve development was $234M before tax — reserves for past claims proved more than enough — even after a $295M addition to asbestos reserves.
Net realized investment losses were $34M before tax ($30M after tax); excluding them, core income was $1,947M, or $9.18 per diluted share.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $118M on Travelers' borrowings, shown below operating income — pre-tax income was $2,369M.
footerNote: Insurer adaptation: revenue here is total reported revenues of $12,412M (premiums earned plus net investment income plus fee income plus other revenues, less realized investment losses). Claims and claim adjustment expenses play the role of cost of revenue, and interest expense is shown below the operating line.
